Triage first-touch (bare-card sweep): queued `pm:queue`, **Bug**, `domain:ui` (lands in this repo's `packages/sdui-parser`). User-visible in the tier the guide recommends by default — any sentence with inline emphasis renders with words run together, silently.

Rule choice, decided at triage: **option (b)** — keep one leading/trailing space when the text run is adjacent to a sibling element (not at the parent's start/end). Mechanical, no block/inline taxonomy invented for a schema tree that has none, and "slightly over-generous inside `<ul>`" is a whitespace nit while (a)'s boundary taxonomy is a design project. Pin the three measured cases + a `<ul>`-shaped control showing the over-generosity is bounded; sweep existing parser snapshots for dependence on the current trimming (a snapshot that changes is part of the fix, reviewed not silently accepted). ⚠️ Twin check required in the PR body: objectstack also carries a `packages/sdui-parser` — establish whether its `parse.ts` shares the `.trim()`; if yes, file the upstream twin card (don't fix cross-repo in this PR). Size S.

**Tier basis.** No path-derived mandate applies (objectui carries no `scripts/pm/`; the objectstack copy of `dispatch-gates.mjs` derives against the wrong tree and is not used). Content judgement: this changes parser **output**, not its accept/reject behaviour, and restores HTML's own whitespace rule rather than inventing one — a `declared = enforced` repair. Clause ② does not trip. Size follows triage's own `S`; tier held at the default judgement档 rather than the floor because "which existing snapshot legitimately changes" is a judgement, not a gate verdict.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main` (now `190fbd01d`, after this round's two merges).** The defect stands: `parse.ts:176-177` still reads

```
const text = this.readTextRun();
const trimmed = text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
```

⚠️ **Line numbers differ from the card's citation** — the card says `:177`, the `readTextRun()` call is at `:176` and the `.trim()` at `:177`. Re-derive from the tree; ⛔ do not cite the card's numbers in the PR.

**⚠️ The twin check triage required is already answered — measured, not assumed.** objectstack **does** carry `packages/sdui-parser/src/parse.ts` and it carries the **identical** construct at **`:168`** (`readTextRun()` at `:167`). So the twin is real and the upstream card is owed. ⛔ Per triage, **do not fix it cross-repo in this PR** — file the upstream twin card with the measurement and link it. Note the line numbers differ between repos (objectui `:177` / objectstack `:168`), so the two files have already drifted; say so in the twin card rather than implying they are a copy.

## ACCEPT — PR #5722 · reviewer of record, `domain:ui` seat, round 17

**Gates read by name at head `051568b5e`:** 19 `success` + 3 `skipped` = 22. Green, all four shards included. Fence clean: 3 files, all `packages/sdui-parser/**` + changeset.

**Triage's snapshot sweep is answered completely, with the control that makes the answer mean something.** The requirement was "sweep existing parser snapshots for dependence on the current trimming; a snapshot that changes is part of the fix, reviewed not silently accepted." The answer: **no snapshot changed and no `-u` run was performed anywhere.** `packages/sdui-parser` holds no snapshot files at all; the repo holds exactly two `.snap` files, both in `packages/components`, and both owning tests were *executed* in a union batch with the `.snap` files unmodified (`git status --porcelain` empty afterwards — and a mismatch fails rather than rewrites). Critically, `vitest list --filesOnly` confirmed all 104 real test files in that directory were **collected**, so neither snapshot test was silently skipped. A "no snapshots changed" claim without that collection check would have been indistinguishable from "the snapshot tests never ran". **Nothing in the repo depended on the old trimming.**

**The twin check came back sharper than my measurement.** I reported the two `parse.ts` files as "already drifted" because the line numbers differ (objectui `:177`, objectstack `:168`). The dev diffed them instead of inferring from the offset: **the only difference is objectui's provenance stamp — an import plus a 9-line block (objectui#4000) — which is exactly the 9-line offset.** The files are otherwise identical. That is a materially better fact than mine: it means the twin is a true copy, not a diverged relative, and it belongs in the upstream card. Filed as **objectstack-ai/objectstack#11148**, cross-linked both ways, correctly *not* fixed cross-repo. The card states its consumer (`packages/lint/src/validate-jsx-pages.ts`) is diagnostics-only so nothing there is visibly broken today — reporting the bound rather than overclaiming — and records that a line-number cherry-pick will not apply.

**Zone 2.4 resolved correctly, and resolved as *not a defect*.** I flagged a second `.trim()` at `:275` and asked whether it was the same bug. It is inside `interpretBrace(raw)`, normalising a braced **attribute's** source text before `JSON.parse` — expression syntax, not the rendered content model, with no separator space at stake. Different defect class, left untouched, and **no card filed** — which is the right call. Filing a card for a non-defect is how a backlog fills with noise.

**Reverse verification, with a control I want to single out.** The fix was committed first, then reverted via `git checkout origin/main -- parse.ts` (revert proven on disk by grep counts in both directions), and the suite went **9 failed / 1 passed** — predicted direction. The one green is `still drops the edge space at the parent's own start and end` — *the half of `.trim()` that was always correct*. That single surviving green is what proves the pin is discriminating rather than blanket: a suite that went 10/10 red would have told us the tests merely detect "the file changed". The render case reproduced the card's exact string, `Akind:'html'page`.

**One more control worth naming:** the three union batches (322 files / 3124 tests) ran at `bded4edf4`, and `git diff --name-only bded4edf4 HEAD` returns **the changeset only** — no source or test file differs. That closes the gap between "what was tested" and "what ships", which a bare test tally never does.

`check:eager-closure` was correctly **not run** with the narrowing declared: it exits 2 as a broken gauge unless the console is vite-built, and this diff adds no import to any package entry so it cannot move that budget. Consistent with this seat's recorded broken-gauge list.

Flipped ready, auto-merge SQUASH. Closes on merge via `Fixes #5661`.
